title: "Docker"
engine: markdown

## Overview

quarto-term can execute commands inside a Docker container instead of a local shell. This is useful for:

- Reproducible builds with a fixed toolbox image
- Running commands that require specific system packages
- Isolating the execution environment from the host

Each document gets its own container: started when the Quarto render begins, automatically removed when it ends. State persists across all `{term}` cells within a single document, just like in local mode.

## Configuration

Set the `docker:` block under `extensions: term:` in your front matter or `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
extensions:
  term:
    docker:
      image: "ubuntu:24.04"
```

The `image` field is required. All other fields are optional. Without a `shell`, the image's own shell is used (see [Shell](#shell)).

## All Docker Options

| Option | Default | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `image` | (required) | Docker image to use |
| `pull` | `missing` | Pull policy: `always`, `missing`, `never` |
| `platform` | (none) | Platform override (e.g., `linux/amd64`) |
| `workdir` | (none) | Working directory inside the container |
| `user` | (none) | Run as `user[:group]` |
| `network` | (docker default) | Network mode (`bridge`, `host`, `none`, or a named network) |
| `memory` | (none) | Memory limit (e.g., `512m`, `2g`) |
| `cpus` | (none) | CPU limit (e.g., `1.5`) |
| `name` | (none) | Container name (useful for debugging) |
| `ports` | `[]` | Port mappings (e.g., `["8080:8080"]`) |
| `volumes` | `[]` | Volume mounts as `host:container[:options]` |
| `env` | `{}` | Environment variables passed to the container |
| `entrypoint` | (image's) | Override the image's `ENTRYPOINT`; an empty value (`entrypoint:` or `""`) clears it |
| `args` | `[]` | Raw extra `docker run` arguments (escape hatch) |

## Examples

### Minimal

```yaml
extensions:
  term:
    docker:
      image: "ubuntu:24.04"
```

The image's default command (`bash`) starts the shell.

### Image Whose Default Command Isn't a Shell

The default command of `python:3.12` is a Python REPL, so set the shell explicitly:

```yaml
extensions:
  term:
    shell: bash
    shell-args: ["--norc", "--noprofile"]
    docker:
      image: "python:3.12"
```

### With Volumes

```yaml
extensions:
  term:
    shell: bash
    shell-args: ["--norc", "--noprofile"]
    docker:
      image: "myorg/toolbox:latest"
      workdir: /workspace
      volumes:
        - "./data:/workspace/data"
        - "./output:/workspace/output"
```

Relative host paths (starting with `.`, like `./data`) are resolved relative to the document's working directory.

### Full-Featured

```yaml
extensions:
  term:
    shell: zsh
    shell-args: ["--no-rcs"]
    prompt: "$"
    timeout: 30.0
    docker:
      image: "myorg/toolbox:latest"
      platform: "linux/amd64"
      pull: missing
      workdir: /home/user
      user: "1000:1000"
      network: none
      memory: "2g"
      cpus: "2.0"
      volumes:
        - "./data:/data"
        - "./images:/images"
      env:
        BAT_THEME: "ansi"
      args: ["--security-opt=no-new-privileges"]
```

### Project-Level Defaults

In `_quarto.yml`, Docker config applies to all documents:

```yaml
extensions:
  term:
    shell: bash
    shell-args: ["--norc", "--noprofile"]
    prompt: "$"
    timeout: 30.0
    docker:
      image: "myorg/toolbox:latest"
      pull: missing
      volumes:
        - "./data:/data"
```

## Volume Mounts

Volume mount syntax follows Docker's `-v` flag: `source:container_path[:options]`. The source is interpreted the same way as by `docker run -v`:

- **Relative host paths** (starting with `.`, like `./data` or `../shared`) are resolved relative to the document's working directory.
- **Absolute host paths** (like `/tmp/cache` or, on Windows, `C:\data`) are used as-is.
- **Named volumes** (a bare name like `cache`) are Docker-managed volumes that outlive the container, so data persists across renders. Docker creates them on first use.
- **Options** like `:ro` (read-only) are passed through.

```yaml
volumes:
  - "./data:/data"           # relative to document directory
  - "/tmp/cache:/cache:ro"   # absolute, read-only
  - "pip-cache:/root/.cache" # named volume
```

To mount a directory next to your document, start the path with `./`. A bare name like `data:/data` mounts a named volume called `data`, not the `data` directory.

## Pull Policies

| Policy | Behavior |
|--------|----------|
| `missing` | Pull only if the image is not already present locally (default) |
| `always` | Always pull, even if the image exists locally |
| `never` | Never pull; fail if the image is not present |

Use `never` for air-gapped environments or when you've pre-pulled images. Use `always` when you want the latest tag on every render.

## Shell {#shell}

### Image's own shell (default)

Without `shell` (or `profile`, or `shell-args`), quarto-term runs the image's default command: its `ENTRYPOINT` and/or `CMD`, just like `docker run -it <image>` would. The shell starts with the image's own configuration (rc files, aliases, prompt), which is usually the environment the image was made for.

The session environment (`PS1`, `PS2`, `env`) is passed with `--env`. If the image has a `CMD`, it's re-run through `env` so that `PS1` and `PS2` survive entrypoint scripts (such as `docker-entrypoint.sh`) that would otherwise drop them:

```
docker run --rm -i -t <options> <image> env PS1='$ ' PS2='> ' <CMD>
```

If the image has only an `ENTRYPOINT` (e.g. `ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/bin/zsh"]`), nothing is appended.

::: {.callout-note}
## Prompts set by the image
If the image's rc files set their own prompt, prompt detection needs to match it: set `prompt` (or `prompt-regex`) accordingly. If the default command isn't an interactive shell at all (e.g. a Python REPL or a server), set `shell` or `profile`.
:::

### Explicit shell

With `shell` (or `profile`, or `shell-args`), that command is appended after the image name and passed to the image's `ENTRYPOINT` as arguments:

```
docker run --rm -i -t <options> <image> env PS1='$ ' PS2='> ' zsh --no-rcs
```

This works for images without an `ENTRYPOINT` and for entrypoint scripts that end with `exec "$@"`. The image must have the configured shell installed.

### `entrypoint`

If the image's `ENTRYPOINT` doesn't run its arguments as a command (for example, when the entrypoint is a shell itself), an explicit `shell` fails to start. Either remove `shell` to use the image's own shell, or clear the entrypoint:

```yaml
docker:
  image: "myorg/toolbox:latest"
  entrypoint:          # empty: clear the image's ENTRYPOINT
```

Any other value replaces the entrypoint (`--entrypoint=<value>`).

When a Docker session fails to start, the error includes a hint based on the image's `ENTRYPOINT` and `CMD`.

## Error Handling

| Scenario | Error Message |
|----------|---------------|
| Docker CLI not installed | `docker not found in PATH` |
| Docker daemon not running | `docker daemon is not running or not accessible` |
| Image not found (pull: never) | `session failed to start: shell process exited unexpectedly` |
| Image pull fails | `failed to pull image '<image>'` |
| Shell not in image | `session failed to start: shell process exited unexpectedly` |
| Explicit `shell` passed to a shell `ENTRYPOINT` | `session failed to start: …` + hint to remove `shell` or set `entrypoint:` |
| Image's default command isn't a shell, or its prompt doesn't match | `session failed to start: timeout waiting for prompt …` + hint to set `shell`, `profile`, or `prompt` |

All errors appear in the rendered output as cell-level error messages (visible in verbose mode on stderr).

## Platform Notes

On Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3) Macs, many images are built for `linux/amd64` only. Use the `platform` option to run them under Rosetta:

```yaml
docker:
  image: "some-amd64-only-image:latest"
  platform: "linux/amd64"
```

This adds `--platform linux/amd64` to the `docker run` command.
